absolute frequency

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A quantitative measure representing the total number of occurrences of a specific item within a given dataset or corpus. This metric serves as a foundational element in frequency analysis, allowing researchers to compare the prevalence of terms or structures across different contexts. Absolute frequency is often contrasted with relative frequency, which expresses occurrences as a proportion of the total number of items in the dataset.

Definición (ES)

Medida cuantitativa que representa el número total de ocurrencias de un ítem específico dentro de un conjunto de datos o un corpus determinado. Esta métrica sirve como un elemento fundamental en el análisis de frecuencia, permitiendo a los investigadores comparar la prevalencia de términos o estructuras en diferentes contextos. La frecuencia absoluta se contrasta a menudo con la frecuencia relativa, que expresa las ocurrencias como una proporción del número total de ítems en el conjunto de datos.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • relative frequency — This term represents the proportion of occurrences of a specific item relative to the total number of items, contrasting with absolute frequency which counts total occurrences.
  • frequency — A broader term that encompasses both absolute and relative frequencies, indicating how often items appear in a dataset.
  • occurrence — Refers to the individual instances of an item within a corpus, which contribute to the calculation of absolute frequency.
  • corpus — The dataset in which absolute frequency is measured, providing the context for analyzing linguistic phenomena.
  • statistical significance — Often assessed using absolute frequencies to determine whether observed patterns in data are meaningful or due to chance.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

"Thus, it is generally useful to convert the absolute frequencies to relative frequencies, abstracting away from the differences in marginal frequencies." (2020_Stefanowitsch, A._Corpus Linguistics A guide to the methodology)

"In determining the ratio, however, we used relative references for both parts of the equation." (2016_Weisser, M._Practical Corpus Linguistics. An Introduction to Corpus-Based Language Analysis)

"This comparison between observed and expected frequencies also provides a foundation for inferential statistics." (2020_Stefanowitsch, A._Corpus Linguistics A guide to the methodology)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "absolute frequency" is widely used in corpus linguistics to provide a straightforward count of occurrences, serving as a basis for further statistical analysis. Its distinction from relative frequency is crucial for accurate interpretation of data, especially in comparative studies.

El término "frecuencia absoluta" se utiliza ampliamente en la lingüística de corpus para proporcionar un conteo directo de ocurrencias, sirviendo como base para un análisis estadístico más profundo. Su distinción de la frecuencia relativa es crucial para una interpretación precisa de los datos, especialmente en estudios comparativos.

accuracy

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A measure of the correctness of a tagging or annotation process, expressed as a percentage of correctly identified elements relative to the total number of elements assessed. This term is often evaluated in the context of different text types, where variations in accuracy can arise due to factors such as text complexity and the representativeness of the training corpus. Accuracy is crucial for ensuring the reliability of linguistic analyses derived from annotated corpora.

Definición (ES)

Medida de la corrección de un proceso de etiquetado o anotación, expresada como un porcentaje de elementos correctamente identificados en relación con el total de elementos evaluados. Este término se evalúa a menudo en el contexto de diferentes tipos de texto, donde las variaciones en la precisión pueden surgir debido a factores como la complejidad del texto y la representatividad del corpus de entrenamiento. La precisión es crucial para garantizar la fiabilidad de los análisis lingüísticos derivados de corpora anotados.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotation — Accuracy is a key metric in evaluating the quality of annotation processes in linguistic corpora.
  • tagger — The performance of a tagger is often assessed through its accuracy, indicating how well it identifies parts of speech or other linguistic features.
  • corpus design — Effective corpus design can influence accuracy by ensuring that the training data is representative of the texts being analyzed.
  • inter-annotator agreement — High accuracy in tagging is often correlated with high inter-annotator agreement, reflecting consistency among different annotators.
  • training corpus — The accuracy of tagging systems can significantly depend on the quality and representativeness of the training corpus used.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

"Although the degree of accuracy was higher than expected, especially in the earlier subperiods, we can see that the tagger is less precise with earlier texts." (source: 2017_Fanego, T., Rodríguez-Puente, et al.)

"The much lower performance we observed for TT in Spanish is, to a large extent, also due to the fact that the domain of the training corpus for Spanish... is less representative and more distant from the fictional texts." (source: 2017_Doval, I.)

"Tagging accuracies below 90% allow neither for a proper direct use of the corpus nor for further linguistic analysis and erode all subsequent processes." (source: 2017_Doval, I.)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "accuracy" is frequently discussed in relation to the performance of various tagging systems, with reported figures varying based on text type and corpus representativeness. In the context of corpus linguistics, accuracy is essential for validating the results of linguistic analyses and ensuring that the data used is reliable.

El término "precisión" se discute frecuentemente en relación con el rendimiento de diversos sistemas de etiquetado, con cifras reportadas que varían según el tipo de texto y la representatividad del corpus. En el contexto de la lingüística de corpus, la precisión es esencial para validar los resultados de los análisis lingüísticos y garantizar que los datos utilizados sean fiables.

alignment

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento del lenguaje

Definition (EN)

The process of matching corresponding segments in source and target texts, typically at the sentence level, is essential in the creation of parallel corpora. This involves using software tools to automatically align texts based on various linguistic features, such as sentence length and lexical anchors. Effective alignment is crucial for ensuring the quality and reliability of multilingual linguistic annotation.

Definición (ES)

El proceso de emparejamiento de segmentos correspondientes en textos fuente y meta, generalmente a nivel de oración, es fundamental en la creación de corpora paralelos. Esto implica el uso de herramientas informáticas para alinear automáticamente los textos en función de diversas características lingüísticas, como la longitud de las oraciones y los anclajes léxicos. Una alineación efectiva es crucial para garantizar la calidad y fiabilidad de la anotación lingüística multilingüe.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • parallel corpus — Alignment is a key process in the construction of parallel corpora, which consist of texts in multiple languages aligned at various levels.
  • annotation — The alignment process often requires linguistic annotation to ensure that the corresponding segments are accurately matched.
  • corpus compilation — Effective alignment is a critical step in the corpus compilation process, particularly for multilingual datasets.
  • sentence level — Most alignment processes occur at the sentence level, which is a common focus in the study of translation and bilingual corpora.
  • translation memory — Alignment is closely related to translation memory systems, which rely on aligned segments to facilitate translation tasks.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

"Software tools can be used to align parallel texts automatically at paragraph, sentence and word level." (2020_Lefer, M. A._Parallel corpora)
"Sentence level alignment is an important part of PTC alignment." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S._History, Features, and Typology of Language Corpora)
"The level of sophistication and accuracy in the task of alignment can thus be refined based on the type of corpus used in text alignment." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S._History, Features, and Typology of Language Corpora)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "alignment" is often used in the context of parallel corpora and translation studies, where it denotes a specific methodological approach to matching text segments. Variations in alignment practices may arise based on the type of corpus and the linguistic features being analyzed.
El término "alineación" se utiliza a menudo en el contexto de los corpora paralelos y los estudios de traducción, donde denota un enfoque metodológico específico para emparejar segmentos de texto. Las variaciones en las prácticas de alineación pueden surgir según el tipo de corpus y las características lingüísticas que se analicen.

annotated corpus

Category / Categoría: Diseño y compilación de corpus

Definition (EN)

A specialized text corpus that includes additional information encoded alongside the primary data, enhancing its utility for linguistic analysis and language technology applications. This information may encompass various extralinguistic features, such as structural markers and linguistic annotations, which are not directly evident from the text itself. The process of annotation adds value to the corpus, allowing for more precise retrieval and analysis compared to unannotated corpora.

Definición (ES)

Un corpus textual especializado que incluye información adicional codificada junto a los datos primarios, lo que aumenta su utilidad para el análisis lingüístico y las aplicaciones de tecnología del lenguaje. Esta información puede abarcar diversas características extralingüísticas, como marcadores estructurales y anotaciones lingüísticas, que no son directamente evidentes del texto mismo. El proceso de anotación añade valor al corpus, permitiendo una recuperación y análisis más precisos en comparación con los corpora no anotados.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotation — Annotation is the process of adding information to a corpus, which is essential for creating an annotated corpus.
  • corpus compilation — Corpus compilation involves the gathering and structuring of texts, which is a prerequisite for developing an annotated corpus.
  • metadata — Metadata provides contextual information about the corpus, complementing the annotations that enhance its analytical capabilities.
  • tagset — A tagset defines the categories of information that can be annotated, which is crucial for the effective use of an annotated corpus.
  • POS tagging — Part-of-speech tagging is a specific type of annotation that contributes to the overall functionality of an annotated corpus.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

"In general, an annotated corpus is a reformed version of a written or spoken corpus in which additional information, which is not directly available from the text itself, is encoded with text from outside." (source: 2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)

"The work is initially carried out manually by experts, who read between the words of texts and identify information to be encoded with the elements of the text." (source: 2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)

"Given the complexity and multi-layeredness of linguistic data, this leads to two main desiderata." (source: 2017_Gries, S. T., Berez, A. L.)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "annotated corpus" encompasses a variety of annotation types, which may vary in complexity and purpose, reflecting the evolving needs of linguistic research and technology. As the field progresses, the methodologies for annotation are also being refined, leading to ongoing discussions about best practices and standards.

El término "corpus anotado" abarca una variedad de tipos de anotación, que pueden variar en complejidad y propósito, reflejando las necesidades en evolución de la investigación lingüística y la tecnología. A medida que el campo avanza, las metodologías para la anotación también se están perfeccionando, lo que lleva a discusiones continuas sobre las mejores prácticas y estándares.

annotation

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A systematic method of adding interpretative information to linguistic data, enhancing its usability for research purposes. This process involves explicit linguistic analysis, distinguishing it from implicit forms of classification that rely on subjective intuitions. Annotation practices are essential for enabling comprehensive searches and addressing complex linguistic phenomena, thereby adding significant value to the corpus.

Definición (ES)

Método sistemático de agregar información interpretativa a datos lingüísticos, mejorando su utilidad para fines de investigación. Este proceso implica un análisis lingüístico explícito, diferenciándose de las formas implícitas de clasificación que dependen de intuiciones subjetivas. Las prácticas de anotación son esenciales para permitir búsquedas exhaustivas y abordar fenómenos lingüísticos complejos, añadiendo así un valor significativo al corpus.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus annotation — Annotation is a specific type of corpus annotation that focuses on adding interpretative layers to linguistic data.
  • tagger — A tagger is a tool used in the annotation process to assign linguistic tags to tokens within a corpus.
  • annotation scheme — An annotation scheme provides the guidelines and conventions that govern how annotations are applied to linguistic data.
  • part-of-speech tagging — Part-of-speech tagging is a specific form of annotation that categorizes words based on their grammatical roles.
  • metadata — Metadata often accompanies annotations, providing contextual information about the data being annotated.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

“The majority view in contemporary corpus linguistics is that ‘adding annotation to a corpus is giving ‘added value’ to it.” (2017_Gries, S. T., Berez, A. L.)
“Corpus annotation involves enormous amounts of work.” (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S.)
“The specific design of annotation systems is codetermined by the specific research interests involved.” (2023_Barth, D., Schnell, S.)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "annotation" encompasses various practices and methodologies, which may differ based on the linguistic level being addressed, such as syntactic or semantic annotation. In Spanish, the term is widely accepted in the field of corpus linguistics, reflecting similar methodological diversity and the importance of explicitness in linguistic analysis.

annotation scheme

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A structured framework that delineates the symbols, definitions, and rules for annotating a corpus. This framework is essential for ensuring that annotations are consistent, recoverable, and based on accessible principles for users. The annotation scheme serves as a methodological guide, contrasting with mere tagging by providing a comprehensive set of guidelines for linguistic analysis.

Definición (ES)

Un marco estructurado que delimita los símbolos, definiciones y reglas para la anotación de un corpus. Este marco es esencial para garantizar que las anotaciones sean consistentes, recuperables y basadas en principios accesibles para los usuarios. El esquema de anotación actúa como una guía metodológica, en contraste con el simple etiquetado, al proporcionar un conjunto integral de directrices para el análisis lingüístico.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotation — The process of adding notes or symbols to a corpus, which is governed by the rules established in the annotation scheme.
  • annotated corpus — A corpus that has been enhanced with annotations according to a specific annotation scheme, making it a valuable resource for linguistic research.
  • tagset — A predefined set of tags used within an annotation scheme to categorize linguistic elements, ensuring uniformity in annotation.
  • coding scheme — A specific type of annotation scheme that outlines how to categorize and interpret data, often used in specialized contexts like anaphora resolution.
  • corpus annotation — The broader practice of adding annotations to a corpus, which is guided by the principles set forth in the annotation scheme.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

The annotation scheme consists of the set of annotative symbols used, their definitions, and the rules and guidelines for their application. (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)

The design of the coding scheme should be informed by awareness of what can be reliably annotated. (2016_Poesio, M., Pradhan, S., Recasens, M., Rodríguez, K., Versley, Y.)

The annotation scheme defines what the problem of anaphora resolution is, and what is the linguistic phenomenon to be learned from the data. (2016_Poesio, M., Pradhan, S., Recasens, M., Rodríguez, K., Versley, Y.)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "annotation scheme" is widely used in the field of corpus linguistics to refer to the systematic approach to annotating linguistic data. Variations in its application may arise depending on the specific linguistic phenomena being studied, as evidenced by different coding schemes for various types of annotations.

El término "esquema de anotación" se utiliza ampliamente en el campo de la lingüística de corpus para referirse al enfoque sistemático de la anotación de datos lingüísticos. Las variaciones en su aplicación pueden surgir dependiendo de los fenómenos lingüísticos específicos que se estudian, como lo evidencian los diferentes esquemas de codificación para varios tipos de anotaciones.

annotation tools

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

Tools designed for the systematic addition of information to textual data, enabling the identification and categorization of linguistic features such as parts of speech, coreference, and semantic roles. These tools can facilitate both automated and manual annotation processes, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of data analysis in corpus linguistics. The distinction between annotation tools and simpler text editors lies in their specialized functionalities tailored for linguistic research.

Definición (ES)

Herramientas destinadas a la adición sistemática de información a datos textuales, que permiten la identificación y categorización de características lingüísticas como las partes del discurso, la correferencia y los roles semánticos. Estas herramientas pueden facilitar tanto procesos de anotación automatizados como manuales, mejorando la eficiencia y precisión del análisis de datos en la lingüística de corpus. La distinción entre herramientas de anotación y editores de texto más simples radica en sus funcionalidades especializadas orientadas a la investigación lingüística.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • annotated corpus — Annotation tools are essential for creating annotated corpora, as they provide the means to systematically label linguistic data.
  • annotation scheme — The effectiveness of annotation tools often depends on the underlying annotation scheme that defines the categories and rules for labeling data.
  • tagger — Taggers are a specific type of annotation tool focused on automatically assigning grammatical tags to words in a text.
  • corpus annotation — Annotation tools are a fundamental component of corpus annotation, facilitating the process of adding linguistic information to corpora.
  • semantic annotation — Some annotation tools specialize in semantic annotation, allowing researchers to mark and analyze the meaning of words and phrases within texts.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

Annotation packages built in, enabling automated annotation of features such as parts-of-speech, parsing and even semantic annotation. (source: 2024_McEnery, T., Brookes, G.)

All the annotation tools discussed here offer the flexibility for adapting to specific annotation goals, as well as the required interaction for making annotation efficient. (source: 2016_Poesio, M. et al.)

They can be employed if own annotation work turns out to be indispensable. (source: 2016_Poesio, M. et al.)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "annotation tools" encompasses a variety of software applications that serve different purposes in linguistic research, from automated tagging to manual annotation support. In Spanish, the term is widely accepted and used in academic contexts, reflecting a growing interest in the integration of technology and linguistic analysis.

AntConc

Category / Categoría: Herramientas y software

Definition (EN)

A software tool designed for corpus linguistics, facilitating the analysis of linguistic data through functions such as concordancing, frequency analysis, and keyword extraction. AntConc allows users to manipulate and visualize corpus data, making it essential for researchers conducting corpus-based studies. Its capabilities contrast with other tools that may focus solely on statistical analysis without providing comprehensive text manipulation features.

Definición (ES)

Una herramienta de software destinada a la lingüística de corpus, que facilita el análisis de datos lingüísticos mediante funciones como la concordancia, el análisis de frecuencia y la extracción de palabras clave. AntConc permite a los usuarios manipular y visualizar datos de corpus, siendo esencial para investigadores que realizan estudios basados en corpus. Sus capacidades contrastan con otras herramientas que pueden centrarse únicamente en el análisis estadístico sin ofrecer características completas de manipulación de texto.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • concordance — AntConc provides a user-friendly interface for generating concordances, which are essential for examining word usage in context.
  • frequency — The software includes features for frequency analysis, allowing researchers to quantify the occurrence of words or phrases within a corpus.
  • keyword — AntConc facilitates keyword analysis, helping users identify significant terms that stand out in a specific corpus compared to a reference corpus.
  • corpus-based — The tool is primarily used in corpus-based research, emphasizing empirical data analysis rather than theoretical speculation.
  • annotation — While AntConc focuses on data analysis, it can work with annotated corpora to enhance the depth of linguistic investigation.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

"If you then want to have this configuration option available permanently, you can overwrite AntConc’s default configuration file by choosing ‘File→Export Settings To File…’." (source)
"Next, change the ‘Tool Preferences’ for ‘Keyword List’ as shown in Figure 9.11." (source)
"AntConc also allows us to see or sort by whether the results occur on left- or right-hand side of the node, and with which frequency." (source)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "AntConc" is widely recognized in the field of corpus linguistics, often associated with user-friendly interfaces for linguistic analysis. Its functionality is particularly valued in educational settings, where it serves as an introductory tool for students learning about corpus methodologies.

El término "AntConc" es ampliamente reconocido en el campo de la lingüística de corpus, a menudo asociado con interfaces amigables para el análisis lingüístico. Su funcionalidad es especialmente valorada en entornos educativos, donde sirve como una herramienta introductoria para estudiantes que aprenden sobre metodologías de corpus.

association measures

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

Statistical tools that quantify the strength of co-occurrence between linguistic units, enabling the identification of significant relationships in corpus data. These measures, such as mutual information and chi-squared, are essential for analyzing collocations and distinguishing between different linguistic patterns. They serve a crucial role in various applications, including collocation studies and keyword analysis, where they help to sort and evaluate linguistic elements based on their statistical significance.

Definición (ES)

Herramientas estadísticas que cuantifican la fuerza de la co-ocurrencia entre unidades lingüísticas, permitiendo la identificación de relaciones significativas en los datos del corpus. Estas medidas, como la información mutua y el chi-cuadrado, son esenciales para analizar las colocaciones y distinguir entre diferentes patrones lingüísticos. Desempeñan un papel crucial en diversas aplicaciones, incluyendo estudios de colocaciones y análisis de palabras clave, donde ayudan a clasificar y evaluar elementos lingüísticos según su significancia estadística.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • collocation — Association measures are often used to determine the strength of collocations by quantifying how frequently words co-occur compared to their expected frequencies.
  • keyword — In keyword analysis, association measures help identify words that are statistically significant within a specific corpus or register.
  • frequency — Association measures rely on frequency data to calculate the likelihood of co-occurrences, making frequency a foundational concept in their application.
  • statistical significance — The validity of association measures is often assessed through statistical significance tests, which determine whether observed co-occurrences are due to chance.
  • normalized frequency — Normalized frequency is frequently used in conjunction with association measures to provide a fair comparison of co-occurrences across different corpus sizes.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

"Association measures quantifying co-occurrence patterns, dispersion scores, keyness scores, etc." (source)
"The inventory of association measures is vast." (source)
"Many of the most widely-used association measures conflate two separate dimensions, namely frequency of the target word in question and the strength of its association to something else." (source)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "association measures" encompasses a variety of statistical techniques that are crucial for analyzing linguistic data in corpus linguistics. While the specific measures may vary in their application and interpretation, they all aim to provide insights into the relationships between words based on their co-occurrence patterns.
El término "medidas de asociación" abarca una variedad de técnicas estadísticas que son cruciales para analizar datos lingüísticos en la lingüística de corpus. Si bien las medidas específicas pueden variar en su aplicación e interpretación, todas tienen como objetivo proporcionar información sobre las relaciones entre palabras basadas en sus patrones de co-ocurrencia.

balanced corpus

Category / Categoría: Diseño y compilación de corpus

Definition (EN)

A type of corpus characterized by an equal representation of texts from various genres or categories, ensuring that no single type dominates the dataset. This concept is often considered essential for achieving representativeness in linguistic research, although the practical realization of a truly balanced corpus is frequently debated among scholars. The notion of balance contrasts with the idea of diversity, which, while related, does not necessarily imply equal representation across categories.

Definición (ES)

Un tipo de corpus que se caracteriza por la representación equitativa de textos de diversos géneros o categorías, asegurando que ningún tipo domine el conjunto de datos. Este concepto se considera esencial para lograr la representatividad en la investigación lingüística, aunque la realización práctica de un corpus verdaderamente equilibrado es objeto de debate entre los académicos. La noción de equilibrio contrasta con la idea de diversidad, que, aunque relacionada, no implica necesariamente una representación equitativa entre categorías.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • representativeness — A balanced corpus aims to achieve representativeness by ensuring equal representation of different genres or categories.
  • general corpus — A balanced corpus can be seen as a specific type of general corpus that emphasizes equal distribution among text types.
  • sample — The design of a balanced corpus involves careful selection of samples from various categories to maintain balance.
  • corpus design — The principles of corpus design are crucial in the creation of a balanced corpus, as they dictate how texts are selected and represented.
  • frequency — The frequency of occurrences in a balanced corpus should reflect the intended equal representation of different categories.
  • diversity — While balance is often sought in corpus design, diversity can serve as a practical alternative when true balance is difficult to achieve.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

"balanced representation will be obtained by using texts from all disciplines and domains in a corpus." (2018_Sekhar Dash, N., Arulmozi, S.)

"In order to determine whether the BNC can be considered a balanced corpus with respect to Speaker Sex, we can compare this observed distribution of speakers to the expected one." (2020_Stefanowitsch, A.)

"balance was achieved by choosing the number of text samples to be included in each category." (2017_Desagulier, G.)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The concept of a balanced corpus is often viewed as an ideal that is challenging to achieve in practice, leading to ongoing discussions about its feasibility and the criteria for balance. Scholars frequently emphasize that while striving for balance is important, it may be more practical to focus on diversity as a proxy for representativeness.

La noción de un corpus equilibrado se considera a menudo un ideal que es difícil de alcanzar en la práctica, lo que lleva a discusiones continuas sobre su viabilidad y los criterios para el equilibrio. Los académicos enfatizan con frecuencia que, si bien es importante aspirar al equilibrio, puede ser más práctico centrarse en la diversidad como un proxy para la representatividad.

Bank of English

Category / Categoría: Corpus de referencia

Definition (EN)

A large digital collection of modern English texts, both written and spoken, designed for the analysis of language form, meaning, grammar, and usage. Developed by COBUILD and the University of Birmingham, it serves as a monitor corpus that continuously updates to reflect current English usage, making it a vital resource for linguistic research and dictionary compilation.

Definición (ES)

Una extensa colección digital de textos en inglés moderno, tanto escritos como hablados, destinada al análisis de la forma, el significado, la gramática y el uso del idioma. Desarrollada por COBUILD y la Universidad de Birmingham, funciona como un corpus de monitorización que se actualiza continuamente para reflejar el uso actual del inglés, convirtiéndose en un recurso vital para la investigación lingüística y la compilación de diccionarios.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • monitor corpus — The Bank of English exemplifies a monitor corpus, as it is designed to grow and adapt over time with new text data.
  • corpus — It is a specific instance of a corpus, focusing on modern English and its varied uses.
  • reference corpus — The Bank of English serves as a reference corpus, providing authoritative examples of language use for linguistic studies.
  • COCA — Both the Bank of English and the Corpus of Contemporary American English (COCA) are significant resources for analyzing contemporary language, though they focus on different varieties of English.
  • corpus compilation — The development of the Bank of English involves corpus compilation techniques to gather diverse text samples.
  • lexicographers — Lexicographers utilize the Bank of English to inform dictionary entries and language resources based on authentic usage.

Fuentes del corpus / Corpus sources

"Overall, the Bank of English provides Digital Text Corpora (Part 2) the most authentic and objective evidence of English that people read, write, speak and hear every day." (source)

"The Bank of English is a huge collection of samples of modern English, both written and spoken, developed in electronic form for analysis of form, meaning, grammar and usage of English words." (source)

"The Bank of English includes several million words of transcribed speech from BBC World Service Radio Broadcasts and American National Public Radio." (source)

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The term "Bank of English" is widely recognized in the field of corpus linguistics as a foundational resource for studying contemporary English. Its ongoing updates and diverse text sources contribute to its relevance, although some scholars may debate its representativeness compared to other corpora.

El término "Bank of English" es ampliamente reconocido en el campo de la lingüística de corpus como un recurso fundamental para el estudio del inglés contemporáneo. Sus actualizaciones continuas y diversas fuentes de texto contribuyen a su relevancia, aunque algunos académicos pueden debatir su representatividad en comparación con otros corpora.

BNC

Category / Categoría: Corpus de referencia

Definition (EN)

A large-scale linguistic resource that encompasses a wide range of written and spoken texts from various genres, designed to represent contemporary British English. The corpus includes both academic and non-academic texts, ensuring a diverse operational domain, which contrasts with more specialized corpora that focus on narrower text types. The BNC serves as a foundational reference corpus for linguistic analysis and research, facilitating the exploration of language use across different contexts.

Definición (ES)

Definition (EN)

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

El intervalo de confianza está inversamente relacionado con el tamaño de la muestra, lo que significa que muestras más grandes producen estimaciones más precisas con intervalos más pequeños. Este concepto es fundamental para determinar la fiabilidad de los análisis de características lingüísticas en estudios de corpus.

A process in natural language processing that involves reducing inflected words to their base or dictionary form, known as a lemma. This technique is essential for tasks such as part-of-speech tagging, as it helps disambiguate words that may serve multiple grammatical functions, thereby enhancing the accuracy of corpus annotations. Lemmatisation differs from stemming, which merely truncates words to their root forms without considering their grammatical context.

Definición (ES)

Proceso en el procesamiento del lenguaje natural que consiste en reducir las palabras flexionadas a su forma base o de diccionario, conocida como lema. Esta técnica es fundamental para tareas como el etiquetado de partes del discurso, ya que ayuda a desambiguar palabras que pueden tener múltiples funciones gramaticales, mejorando así la precisión de las anotaciones en un corpus. La lematización se diferencia del stemming, que simplemente recorta las palabras a sus raíces sin considerar su contexto gramatical.

  • tokenisation — Tokenisation is a prerequisite for lemmatisation, as it involves breaking text into individual tokens that can then be lemmatised.
  • annotation — Lemmatisation is a specific type of annotation that focuses on the morphological aspect of words within a corpus.
  • lemma — The lemma is the base form to which inflected words are reduced during the lemmatisation process.
  • corpus annotation — Lemmatisation is a critical component of corpus annotation, enhancing the usability and analytical potential of linguistic data.

lexeme

Category / Categoría: Procesamiento del lenguaje

Definition (EN)

A fundamental unit of meaning in a language, distinguished from its various inflected forms or wordforms. Lexemes represent the abstract concept of a word, encompassing all its grammatical variations, such as tense or number, which are not considered separate entities. This distinction is crucial in corpus linguistics, where understanding the relationship between lexemes and their forms aids in analyzing linguistic patterns and structures.

Definición (ES)

Unidad fundamental de significado en una lengua, que se distingue de sus diversas formas flexionadas o wordforms. Los lexemas representan el concepto abstracto de una palabra, abarcando todas sus variaciones gramaticales, como el tiempo o el número, que no se consideran entidades separadas. Esta distinción es crucial en la lingüística de corpus, donde comprender la relación entre los lexemas y sus formas ayuda a analizar patrones y estructuras lingüísticas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • token — A token is an instance of a lexeme in a text, highlighting the difference between the abstract concept of a lexeme and its concrete occurrences.
  • lemma — A lemma is a specific form of a lexeme used as a headword in dictionaries, serving as a representative form for all its inflected variations.
  • word class — Word classes categorize lexemes based on their grammatical function, such as nouns or verbs, which is essential for understanding their usage in corpus analysis.
  • collocation — Collocations involve the habitual co-occurrence of lexemes, revealing semantic relationships and usage patterns that are significant in corpus studies.
  • frequency — The frequency of a lexeme in a corpus provides insights into its usage and relevance within a specific linguistic context, contrasting with the frequency of individual tokens.

lexical bundles

Category / Categoría: Léxico y fraseología

Definition (EN)

A specific type of multi-word sequence characterized by its recurrent occurrence within a corpus, typically defined as sequences of words that appear together frequently and serve particular grammatical or discourse functions. Methodologically, lexical bundles are operationalized based on frequency thresholds, such as appearing at least ten times per million words across multiple texts, distinguishing them from other n-grams that may not exhibit the same stability or functional significance in discourse.

Definición (ES)

Secuencias de palabras compuestas por varias unidades léxicas que aparecen con frecuencia en un corpus y que cumplen funciones gramaticales o discursivas específicas. Los "lexical bundles" se definen metodológicamente mediante umbrales de frecuencia, como la aparición de al menos diez veces por millón de palabras en varios textos, lo que los distingue de otros n-grams que pueden no mostrar la misma estabilidad o relevancia funcional en el discurso.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • n-gram — A lexical bundle is a specific type of n-gram that is defined by its frequency and functional significance in discourse.
  • frequency — The identification of lexical bundles relies on their frequency of occurrence within a corpus, which is a key methodological criterion.
  • collocation — While collocations refer to words that frequently occur together, lexical bundles encompass longer sequences that may include multiple collocations.
  • corpus — Lexical bundles are derived from the analysis of a corpus, making the corpus essential for their identification and study.
  • text type — The nature of lexical bundles can vary significantly across different text types, reflecting the contextual usage of language.

log-likelihood

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A statistical measure used to assess the association between two categorical variables, calculated by comparing observed frequencies to expected frequencies under a null hypothesis. This method is particularly favored in collocational research for its reliability with small samples, contrasting with the chi-squared test, which may overestimate rare events. The log-likelihood ratio test is recognized for its robustness in linguistic data analysis, as it accounts for the independence of observations more effectively than some alternative measures.

Definición (ES)

Una medida estadística utilizada para evaluar la asociación entre dos variables categóricas, calculada al comparar frecuencias observadas con frecuencias esperadas bajo una hipótesis nula. Este método es especialmente valorado en la investigación sobre colocaciones por su fiabilidad con muestras pequeñas, en contraste con la prueba de chi-cuadrado, que puede sobreestimar eventos raros. La prueba de razón de verosimilitud es reconocida por su solidez en el análisis de datos lingüísticos, ya que tiene en cuenta la independencia de las observaciones de manera más efectiva que algunas medidas alternativas.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • chi-squared — The log-likelihood test is often preferred over the chi-squared test due to its greater reliability with small sample sizes and rare events.
  • association measures — Log-likelihood is a specific type of association measure used to quantify the strength of the relationship between words in collocational studies.
  • frequency — Log-likelihood calculations are based on observed and expected frequencies, making frequency a fundamental component of its methodology.
  • collocation — This measure is widely applied in collocation research to determine the strength of word associations within a corpus.
  • statistical significance — Log-likelihood is used to establish statistical significance in linguistic data analysis, providing insights into the relationships between variables.

markup language

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A system for annotating a document in a way that is syntactically distinguishable from the text itself, allowing for the representation of structural and semantic information. Markup languages, such as SGML and XML, facilitate the encoding of linguistic features without altering the original content, thus preserving the integrity of the text for analysis. This contrasts with annotation, which often involves adding interpretative information rather than structural tags.

Definición (ES)

Un sistema para anotar un documento de manera que sea sintácticamente distinguible del texto mismo, permitiendo la representación de información estructural y semántica. Los lenguajes de marcado, como SGML y XML, facilitan la codificación de características lingüísticas sin alterar el contenido original, preservando así la integridad del texto para su análisis. Esto contrasta con la anotación, que a menudo implica la adición de información interpretativa en lugar de etiquetas estructurales.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • tagger — A tool that may utilize markup languages to apply tags to linguistic data, enhancing the analysis process.
  • corpus annotation — The process that may involve markup languages to enrich texts with additional linguistic information.

Unlike static corpora, a monitor corpus is intended to grow, reflecting the evolving usage of language and lexical items.

morphological annotation

Category / Categoría: Anotación y marcado

Definition (EN)

A type of corpus annotation that involves the systematic labeling of word forms to indicate their morphological components and grammatical functions. Morphological annotation is often contrasted with parts-of-speech tagging, which focuses solely on categorizing words into classes without detailing their internal structure.

La anotación morfológica se contrasta a menudo con el etiquetado de partes del discurso, que se centra únicamente en clasificar las palabras sin detallar su estructura interna.

  • tagger — A tagger is a tool that may be used to perform morphological annotation by automatically assigning morphological labels to word forms.

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

Existen variantes de la información mutua que pueden producir resultados diferentes, lo que subraya la importancia de la consistencia metodológica en estudios comparativos.

Category / Categoría: Léxico y fraseología

Definition (EN)

A sequence of n words that occur together in a specific order, where 'n' can represent any number greater than one. This concept is commonly applied in natural language processing to model the probability of word sequences, distinguishing it from unigrams and bigrams, which refer to sequences of one and two words, respectively. N-grams are particularly useful for tasks such as speech recognition and machine translation, where understanding the context of word sequences is crucial.

Definición (ES)

Los n-grams son especialmente útiles para tareas como el reconocimiento de voz y la traducción automática, donde la comprensión del contexto de las secuencias de palabras es crucial.

node word

Category / Categoría: Léxico y fraseología

Definition (EN)

A lexical item that serves as a reference point within a corpus for analyzing the co-occurrence and contextual relationships of surrounding words. This term is often employed in statistical analyses to determine the degree of relatedness between words based on their proximity to the node word, contrasting with broader terms like "collocation" that may not specify a focal point. The methodological significance of the node word lies in its role in facilitating the exploration of linguistic patterns and structures within a given text.

La importancia metodológica del nodo radica en su función para facilitar la exploración de patrones y estructuras lingüísticas dentro de un texto determinado.

normalized frequency

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A statistical measure that expresses the frequency of a linguistic unit relative to a standard size of the corpus, typically per 10,000 words. This normalization allows for fair comparisons between different corpus samples of varying sizes, highlighting distributional similarities or differences. Unlike raw frequency, which merely counts occurrences, normalized frequency provides a standardized metric that accounts for corpus size.

Definición (ES)

Una medida estadística que expresa la frecuencia de una unidad lingüística en relación con un tamaño estándar del corpus, típicamente por cada 10,000 palabras. Esta normalización permite comparaciones justas entre diferentes muestras de corpus de tamaños variables, destacando similitudes o diferencias en la distribución. A diferencia de la frecuencia absoluta, que solo cuenta ocurrencias, la frecuencia normalizada proporciona una métrica estandarizada que considera el tamaño del corpus.

Relación con otros términos del glosario / Relation to other glossary terms

  • corpus — The concept of normalized frequency is inherently linked to the corpus, as it relies on the total word count of the corpus to calculate the frequency measure.
  • keyword — Normalized frequency is often used in keyword analysis to identify significant terms that appear more frequently than expected in a specific corpus compared to a reference corpus.
  • dispersion — While normalized frequency measures how often a term occurs, dispersion assesses how evenly that frequency is distributed across the corpus, providing complementary insights.

Definition (EN)

Unlike absolute frequency, which counts raw occurrences, relative frequency provides a context-sensitive perspective that aids in identifying patterns and trends in linguistic research.

statistical significance

Category / Categoría: Frecuencia y estadística

Definition (EN)

A measure indicating that the results obtained from a sample are unlikely to be due to chance, thus allowing for generalization to a larger population with a specified level of certainty. Este indicador permite a los investigadores evaluar la riqueza léxica y está influenciado por el tamaño de la muestra, ya que muestras más grandes tienden a generar proporciones de tipo-token más altas. Se contrasta con las proporciones de hapax legomena, que se centran específicamente en las palabras que ocurren solo una vez en un texto determinado.

Nota terminológica / Terminological note

The z-score is widely used in various fields, including linguistics, to standardize scores for comparison. Its application may vary depending on the context, such as in corpus linguistics for analyzing word frequencies or in broader statistical analyses.

El z-score se utiliza ampliamente en diversos campos, incluida la lingüística, para estandarizar puntuaciones para su comparación. Su aplicación puede variar según el contexto, como en la lingüística de corpus para analizar frecuencias de palabras o en análisis estadísticos más amplios.
